from_notes: Water (Hydrophily): Water carries pollen from one plant to another, typically in aquatic plants. E.g., vallisneria, seagrasses.
x: In Vallisneria the male flowers break off and float up to the water surface, where water currents carry them to the female flowers raised on long stalks, so the whole male flower travels. In Zostera (a seagrass) only long pollen grains are released and carried under water; Nymphaea (water lily) is insect-pollinated.
source: PMF General Science 03 (src/science-tech/pmf-general-science-03.txt) p.38 (hydrophily: Vallisneria, seagrasses); detached-male-flower detail: general knowledge, not checked

from_notes: Open Circulatory System: This circulatory system, found in invertebrates like insects, allows blood to flow freely through the body cavity and bathe the organs in the fluid.
x: The cockroach, an insect (arthropod), has an open circulatory system: haemolymph is pumped into open sinuses (haemocoel) and bathes the organs. Fish, snakes and earthworms have closed circulatory systems with blood kept inside vessels.
source: PMF General Science 02 (src/science-tech/pmf-general-science-02.txt) p.4 and p.34 (open system in arthropods and molluscs); PMF General Science 01 p.90 (arthropods: open circulatory system)

from_notes: Insects have a network of tubes (tracheae) that transport air within their bodies.
x: Insects such as the cockroach breathe through tracheae: air enters by spiracles and the tracheal tubes take it straight to the tissues. The earthworm breathes through its moist skin, the frog by skin and lungs, and fish by gills.
source: PMF General Science 02 (src/science-tech/pmf-general-science-02.txt) p.20; OnlyIAS NCERT Science 10 (src/science-tech/onlyias-ncert-science-tech-10.txt) p.6 (cockroach tracheal system, spiracles)

from_notes: Earthworms and frogs breathe through their moist skin (cutaneous respiration). However, frogs also have lungs for respiration.
x: Cutaneous respiration (gas exchange through moist skin) is seen in the earthworm and the frog; the frog also uses lungs. Fish breathe by gills and humans by lungs, so every other pair includes a non-cutaneous breather.
India's national tree is the Indian banyan, Ficus benghalensis. Ficus religiosa is the peepal (sacred fig), Ficus elastica the rubber fig and Ficus racemosa the cluster fig (gular).

from_notes: Glyptotermes chiraharitae (APPSC PYQ): a dampwood termite from Malabar WLS (Kakkayam), Kozhikode, Kerala; described in 2016; name from Sanskrit chiraharita = evergreen.
x: Glyptotermes chiraharitae is a new dampwood termite (family Kalotermitidae) described in 2016 from the evergreen forests of Malabar Wildlife Sanctuary, Kozhikode, Kerala; 'chiraharita' is Sanskrit for evergreen. It is not a deer, plant or butterfly.

x: Worker bees are sterile females that do the colony's work: foraging for nectar and pollen, making honey and wax, nursing the brood and guarding the hive. Only the queen lays eggs, and the drones (males) mate with her, so guarding is only one of the workers' many tasks.
source: PMF General Science 04 (src/science-tech/pmf-general-science-04.txt) p.18 (queen and workers are diploid females, drones haploid males); Shankar Environment 09 (src/environment/shankar-environment-09.ocr.txt) p.2 (hives cannot survive without the foraging worker bees); worker duties: general knowledge, not checked
